newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia key stock index falls to 30-month low.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia key stock index falls to 30-month low.

text.p: Malaysia's key stock market barometer fell 3.40 percent in early afternoon trading to a 30-month low on persistent selling of blue chip issues.
At 0732 GMT, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Composite Index was down 30.96 points to 879.22, its lowest intraday level since January 27, 1995 when it hit 836.93.
"People are expecting the ringgit to be fall further. that's what's further dampening the market," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
The ringgit had fallen to its all-time lowest level on Friday, when it broke the 2.80 ringgit level against the U.S. dollar.
"There are also fears that Bank Negara will come out with new measures to curb speculation on the ringgit. I don't see much of local funds buying. They fear a ringgit bashing," he said.
Dealers said they saw the next support level for the index at around the 850-point mark.
"People don't believe that the market has stabilised yet. A lot of people I talked to said they will come in at 850. But most of the selling has tapered down," said a Jardine Fleming trader.
